properties.label: RETROSPECTIVE FORECAST · FROM THE RECONSTRUCTED FRONT · NOT VALIDATED

diagnostics.initialFrontNote: The entire initial mask boundary is a source of spread; only cells reached within the previous 12 hours (according to the reconstruction) could be recent front. The remainder reactivates old edges.
diagnostics.note: The final footprint is known only retrospectively; the forecast is not clipped to it.

weather.source: Open-Meteo historical archive (ERA5-based reanalysis), one grid point, 10 m
weather.convention: windFromDeg = meteorological direction FROM which the wind blows (degrees); spread is towards windFromDeg + 180.
weather.note: Constant within each hour, integrated hour by hour; rhPct, tempC and gustMps are context only and do not change the rate.

assumptions.seed: No artificial ignition point: spread starts from every arrival-reconstructed cell with t ≤ timeUtc; its boundary is the initial front.
assumptions.fuel: assumed uniform fuel (factor 1); no fuel map or fuel moisture input
assumptions.wind: historical hourly wind (Open-Meteo, one point), constant within each UTC hour; meteorological windFrom convention, spread towards +180°
assumptions.relativeHumidity: context only; does not change spread
assumptions.equation: Multi-source minimum travel time (Dijkstra, 8 neighbours) from ALL reconstructed mask cells with t ≤ timeUtc; rate = base·fuel·W·S, W = exp(KW·v·cos(bearing − windTowards)), S = clamp(exp(KS·dz/dist), S_MIN, S_MAX); wind follows the current UTC hour and is integrated in segments across each hourly boundary (FIFO).

limitations: Retrospective and NOT validated: compared with the satellite reconstruction, not independently observed ground truth.
Reconstructed reference: first VIIRS detection within 400 m, not the exact front; overestimates the published area (×1.53 on 25 August and ×1.38 on 31 August).
The reference uses the final footprint retrospectively: the reconstruction cannot grow outside the final perimeter, so all modelled expansion outside it counts as overprediction.
The initial mask inherits the limitations of the reconstruction; it is not a mapped fire front.
Heuristic model using simulation.py coefficients (neither fitted nor validated); not Rothermel or FARSITE; no spotting, suppression, firebreaks or fuel changes.
Uniform fuel (factor 1) is assumed throughout the domain, including outside the historical footprint; there is no fuel map or fuel moisture input.
Wind from ONE model point (Open-Meteo historical Best Match, 10 m), uniform across the domain and constant within each hour; not a local measurement. Gusts are not used.
Relative humidity and temperature are context only: they do not change the spread rate.
200 m DEM (AWS Terrarium z12, 5×5 mean): local slopes are smoothed; vertical accuracy is unverified.
Results depend on assumptions fixed before measurement: parameters were not tuned to improve IoU.

Initial front = the ENTIRE boundary of the reconstructed mask treated as active. This reactivates old edges that may no longer have been burning; it is not an observed front and partly explains the overprediction. The reference was not used to select active edges.

provenance.method: Multi-source minimum travel time (Dijkstra, 8 neighbours) from ALL reconstructed mask cells with t ≤ timeUtc; rate = base·fuel·W·S, W = exp(KW·v·cos(bearing − windTowards)), S = clamp(exp(KS·dz/dist), S_MIN, S_MAX); wind follows the current UTC hour and is integrated in segments across each hourly boundary (FIFO).

dem.resampling: mean of 5x5 nearest-pixel samples (+-80 m) per 200 m cell; rows north-to-south (same as the 149x158 base DEM)

provenance.referenceBias: The reconstruction exceeds the published area by ×1.53 (25 August) and ×1.38 (31 August); the first detection is not the exact arrival time.
provenance.weatherSource: Open-Meteo historical archive (ERA5-based reanalysis), one grid point, 10 m
